what_went_right: The two-step review (review-gatherer bundle -> independent code-reviewer verdict) caught a real regression in the FIRST draft before it ever landed on main: excluding the failed tab id could empty the candidate pool for the single-tab case, turning a recoverable transient failure into an immediate zero-retry error. .review/last-verdict.json confirms should_fix_count: 3, critical_count: 0 and the fix was folded into the same single commit (c51edb0) that shipped -- no follow-up fixup commit was needed, unlike this project's prior bg-prefetch saga which took 3 commits to fully land the equivalent class of fix.

proxyFetch and proxyFetchBinary both got the identical exclude-Set/attempts-loop treatment in the same commit -- no symmetric-fix miss of the kind this project's memory has repeatedly flagged (new-pre-step-in-send-path-must-propagate-to-retry-path, symmetric-invariant-fixes-must-touch-both-sides). The shared pool-fallback logic lives once, centrally, in findProxyTab, so both callers inherit the fix uniformly rather than needing two independent patches.

Tests were written for both directions of the regression, not just the original bug: 'falls through to a second open substack.com tab when the first fails injection' (multi-tab) AND 'retries the SAME tab on a transient failure when it's the only one open' (single-tab, the reviewer's regression catch). Full suite 577/577 green after the fix, verified independently in this retro.

The user-facing error message was upgraded from Chrome's raw, unactionable 'manifest must request permission' text to a message that tells the user exactly what to do (open/refresh https://substack.com/chat), with a dedicated test asserting the new copy, not just that SOME error is thrown.
what_went_wrong: This is literally iteration N+1 on the same lib/api.js proxy-tab surface: commit 114170a (2026-06-06) already shipped a fix for this exact live error message ('executeScript failed (tab closed?)...') via a bare retry. That retry only covered the narrow TOCTOU race window -- because chrome.tabs.query returns tabs in stable order, a persistently (not just transiently) dead tab would get reselected by the retry and fail again. The user hit the same raw error a second time 5+ weeks later, meaning the June 6 fix was incomplete for the common case it was supposed to solve, and that incompleteness was never caught until it recurred live.

The FIRST draft of the July 15 fix introduced a real regression of its own in the process of fixing the June 6 gap: excluding the failed tab unconditionally would empty the candidate pool and return zero retries for a user with exactly one Substack tab open (the majority deployment), which is worse than the pre-fix behavior for that exact case. This was caught by the independent reviewer, not by the work-agent's own reasoning before writing the code -- the same 'harden one path without auditing what happens to the degenerate/common case' shape this project's memory has now recorded four separate times across different features.

Test coverage is asymmetric between the two proxy functions: proxyFetch got 4 dedicated regression tests (multi-tab fallthrough, single-tab-still-retries, final actionable error, no-tab-open distinct message) but proxyFetchBinary got only 1 (multi-tab fallthrough). The single-tab-retry-still-works and final-actionable-error paths for proxyFetchBinary's own attempts-loop wrapper are exercised only indirectly (via the shared findProxyTab tests through the proxyFetch describe block), not directly for the binary path.
three_whys: Why 1: On 2026-07-15 a user again hit the raw, unactionable Chrome error ('executeScript failed (tab closed?): Cannot access contents of the page. Extension manifest must request permission...') surfacing straight into the chat UI -- the exact same error message BetterSSC had already shipped a fix for 5+ weeks earlier (commit 114170a, 2026-06-06).

Why 2: The June 6 fix's retry (re-invoke findProxyTab() with no exclusion after invalidating the cache) only helped inside a narrow TOCTOU race window. Because chrome.tabs.query returns tabs in stable order, a tab that was persistently unreachable (closed, navigated away, backgrounded/discarded) would simply be reselected by the retry and fail again -- the retry mechanism never tried a DIFFERENT tab, so it added no real recovery value once a second live Substack tab existed but wasn't being considered.

Why 3 (root cause): The July 15 fix correctly diagnosed why 2 and set out to exclude already-tried tab ids so a different, live tab would get picked on retry -- but the first draft implemented the exclusion unconditionally, without an explicit branch for the case where filtering empties the candidate pool. That is precisely the numerically dominant real-world deployment (exactly one Substack tab open), so the hardening silently regressed the common case it was meant to protect. This is the same recurring authoring gap this project's memory already names in three other incidents (new-cursor-consumer-needs-symmetric-mutex-not-one-way-priority, symmetric-invariant-fixes-must-touch-both-sides, new-pre-step-in-send-path-must-propagate-to-retry-path): a partial mechanism that looks like it covers the case, but wasn't checked against the degenerate/most-common input, and was only caught by an INDEPENDENT reviewer rather than by the work-agent's own pre-write reasoning.

drift_checklist.finding: none -- all 3 should-fix findings from .review/last-verdict.json (critical_count: 0, should_fix_count: 3) were folded into the single landed commit: the single-tab-pool-empty regression (pool fallback fix), the untested proxyFetchBinary fallthrough path (new fallthrough test added), and order-fragile test mock hygiene (beforeEach resets chrome.tabs.get/query/executeScript mocks so tests don't leak state between runs).

No retry on executeScript failure. If the cached tab navigated off substack.com or was closed between findProxyTab() and executeScript() (TOCTOU), the whole call died. Now we invalidate the cache, re-find a tab, and try once more before throwing.

The bug class: when you add a SECOND consumer of an existing single-consumer-protected resource, you don't just need to check the lock — you need to TAKE it the same way the existing consumer does. The polling check is necessary but not sufficient.

action_items.description: test/api-proxy-tab.test.mjs gives proxyFetch (via fetchInbox) 4 dedicated regression tests -- multi-tab fallthrough, single-tab-still-retries-on-transient-failure, final actionable error message, and no-tab-open distinct message -- but proxyFetchBinary (via putChatMediaBinary) only got 1 (multi-tab fallthrough), even though it wraps the same tried-Set/attempts-loop pattern around the same shared findProxyTab. Add the missing 3 tests to proxyFetchBinary's describe block so a future edit to its own retry-loop wrapper (not just findProxyTab) gets the same regression coverage proxyFetch has.

action_items.title: Treat exclusion-based retry hardening as incomplete until the empty-pool branch is explicit and tested
action_items.description: Any retry/failover/candidate-selection logic that maintains an exclusion set of already-tried/already-failed items (a proxy-tab picker excluding dead tabs, a connection-pool retry excluding a dead node, a load-balancer failover excluding a tripped backend) has the same latent trap: filtering out the failed candidate can empty the pool, and the single/only-candidate case is usually the numerically DOMINANT real-world deployment, not a rare edge case. The fix pattern is mechanical and cheap to apply everywhere it recurs: after writing the exclusion filter, explicitly decide and test what happens when it returns empty (fall back to the unfiltered set, or surface a distinct 'no alternative' error) rather than leaving the empty-array behavior implicit. This is a generalizable software-engineering principle, not specific to BetterSSC's proxy-tab architecture, and is not covered by any existing promoted CLAUDE.md lesson.
